title: Very Low Density Lipoprotein Turnover in Young and Elderly Individuals
brief_summary: Intrahepatic and intramyocellular lipid concentrations are elevated in elderly individuals relative to young people, despite no significant difference in fasting plasma TAG concentrations. Our general hypothesis is that the increase in intrahepatic fat with age results from reduced VLDL turnover, and therefore elderly individuals in this study will display lower VLDL turnover rates than young individuals. The aims of this study are a) to compare VLDL turnover in young and elderly individuals, and b) to compare a bolus method and a constant infusion method of assessing VLDL turnover.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 to 35 years, or 60 to 75 years.
* Body mass index ≤ 27 kg•m2
* Ability to sign informed consent.
* Score of ≥26 for Mini-Mental State Exam

Exclusion Criteria:

* Diabetics (plasma glucose concentration \>200 mg/dl at 2 hr after oral intake of 75 g glucose).
* Fasting plasma triacylglycerol concentration above 500 mg/dl
* Kidney disease.
* Liver disease.
* Bleeding disorders.
* Anaemia (Hb \< 13 g/dl in males or \< 12 g/dl in females).
* Endocrine disease (with the exception of well-regulated hypothyroidism).
* Positive hepatitis or HIV screens.
* Alcohol (CAGE questionnaire; abnormal liver enzyme values) or drug abuse (amphetamines, cocaine, opioids, marijuana).
* Lipid altering agents.
* Score of \<26 for Mini-Mental State Exam
study_population: Healthy individuals from the Galveston area.
